My name is Catherine Parker, and I'm a violence prevention specialist at Laws, Domestic Violence, and Sexual Assault Services. For more than 30 years, Laws has been a leader in primary prevention working to stop violence before it starts. Through education, outreach, and partnerships, we empower youth, parents, families, and professionals with the knowledge and skills to build healthy relationships and create a safer Loudoun County. Our prevention programming is comprehensive and evidence-informed. We provide workshops on healthy relationships, consent and

body safety, and bystander intervention, ensuring young people have the tools to recognize red flags, set boundaries, and support their peers. In the last fiscal year alone, our team conducted 72 prevention and outreach activities with youth and youth serving professionals, reaching more than 2,600 young

people and professionals, more than tripling our impact from the previous year. Prevention education does not stop at the classroom. Laws trains coaches, teachers, social workers, youth mentors, and law enforcement, ensuring that trusted adults can recognize warning signs and intervene early.

And through our program, Loud and Axe, as well, we've been working with alcohol serving establishments to prevent sexual violence in social spaces by training staff and bystander intervention. Prevention works. By investing in education and early intervention and strong partnerships, Laws is changing norms, reducing risk factors, and creating a community where violence is not tolerated. Together, we can build on these successes, leveraging years of accumulating best practices established through Laws' prevention efforts. Strengthening what's working means reinforcing, supporting, and promoting existing prevention efforts and proven strategies.

Together, we can continue to stop violence before it begins and build a future where every young person grows up safe, informed, and empowered in Loudoun County. Together, we can ensure Loudoun County remains a leader in compassionate, effective, survivor-centered services, setting a standard for communities across the Commonwealth.

My name is Diana, and I'm the Community Services Director at Laws and the co-facilitator of the Loudoun Domestic Abuse Response Team, also known as DART. For over two decades, DART has been the backbone of Loudoun County's Coordinated Community Response, the CCR, to domestic violence. Established in 2005, DART was built on national best practices, bringing together law enforcement, the courts, social services, mental health providers, and laws to ensure a seamless survivor-centered response.

DART has driven transformative change, strengthening the community's response to domestic violence, and expanding support for survivors in Loudoun County. We have been successful in our work. Our multidisciplinary collaboration has led to creation of dedicated domestic violence detectives, specialized domestic violence probation officers, and the implementation of the Lethality Assessment Protocol, or LAP, which has resulted in a 68% reduction in intimate partner homicides since the implementation in 2016.

In 2023, Loudoun County DART was instrumental in shaping statewide policy, successfully advocating for the addition of suffocation to Virginia's strangulation statute. This legislative change was a direct result of the expertise and collaboration within our DART, ensuring that our justice system recognizes the profound seriousness of non-fatal strangulation and suffocation in domestic violence cases.

Over time and through an evolving community landscape, DART has remained strong, active, and effective, convening monthly meetings, addressing system gaps, and providing training and resources to key partners. Loudoun's coordinated model has been recognized statewide and nationally as a leader and survivor-centered collaborative domestic violence response. As Loudoun considers ways to strengthen services, it's critical to build upon the existing success and infrastructure of the DART. The foundation is in place and has the opportunity to leverage the experience and insights of laws and our partners from our decades of co-facilitating and engaging in DART to result in even better outcome and services.

By investing in what is proven to be effective, together we can enhance the coordination of services when all partners work in alignment. Together we have an opportunity to build upon 21 years of DART success, ensuring that every survivor receives the best possible care in the most effective and collaborative way. Together, we can ensure Loudoun County remains a leader in compassionate, effective survivor services, setting a standard for communities across the Commonwealth.
